title: Dense suborders and equivalent forcing presentations

based_on.title: Lecture Notes on Iterated Forcing
based_on.pages: 20 (§5, Definition 5.1, Lemma 5.2 and Remark 5; Vienna winter term 2021)

summary: Pass between dense forcing orders by explicit generic-filter and name translations, with finite binary strings as a Cohen presentation.
abstract: Cohen forcing can be described by arbitrary finite binary assignments or by finite binary strings. The string conditions are dense: every finite assignment can be extended by filling its missing positions. More generally, a dense inherited suborder carries exactly the same generic filters after taking traces or upward closures, and explicit recursive translations of names show that corresponding filters give the very same extension. These constructions work even when the smaller order has no largest condition. A change of condition labels also preserves the extension when it both preserves and reflects order; a two-point example shows why preserving order alone is insufficient.
